Brash

BRASH -- of disputed origin; most sources trace it only to mid-1900s American slang, with no clear Latin or Greek root to follow further back. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Brash is self-assertive in a rude, tactless way.

The new player's brash trash-talk toward veteran opponents twice his age did not sit well with either team.

Worked Example

On his very first day, the transfer student loudly announced to the whole class that their previous teacher 'clearly had no idea what she was doing.'

Brash combines boldness with a rude, tactless edge -- announcing a harsh opinion about a respected teacher to an entire class on your first day is bold in the worst possible way.

How Brash Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

cocky

cocky: overconfident in a way that annoys others

impudent

impudent: boldly disrespectful or rude, especially to someone owed respect

Antonyms

polite

polite: having good manners; considerate of others

reserved

reserved: slow to reveal opinions or feelings; restrained

How Strong Is It? — cocky → brash → impudent

cocky vs. brash

cocky vs. brash: Cocky is a casual word for annoying overconfidence, often about one's own skill, while brash adds an active, rude edge in how someone treats others.

impudent vs. brash

impudent vs. brash: Impudent is more formal than brash and specifically stresses disrespect toward someone who is owed more consideration, such as an elder or a superior.
